The '''Qiraash''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Near-Human]]s with [[Color/Legends|pale]], pink skin. Their large craniums were bald except for [[Hair/Legends|hair]] growing from the back of the neck. Some Qiraash plaited this into elaborate top-knots. [[Leesub Sirln/Legends|Leesub Sirln]] was a Qiraash with limited powers of [[Precognition/Legends|precognition]]. [[High Inquisitor]] [[Antinnis Tremayne]] encountered Sirln and declared her a [[Force Adept]]. In order to avoid [[Prison/Legends|imprisonment]] or [[Death/Legends|death]] at the hand of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire's]] [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]], Sirln went into hiding on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Qiraash_profile.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Leesub Sirln, in profile]]
The Qiraash were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Near-Human]]s.<ref name="CCG" /> They were [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]]&mdash;having two [[Limb/Legends|arms]] and two legs&mdash;but their [[Color/Legends|pale]], pink skin and large craniums set them apart from [[Human/Legends|Humans]]. The Qiraash head was bald except for curly [[Hair/Legends|hair]] growing from the nape of the neck. Some Qiraash grew tufts of this hair long and wore it in elaborate coiffures. For example, the Qiraash [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Leesub Sirln/Legends|Leesub Sirln]] plaited it into a top-knot at the crown of her skull. From here, three smaller plaits ran toward the front of her skull; one each running along the sides of the head and down past the front of the [[Ear/Legends|ears]], and the third running down the center of the forehead and ending just above the eyebrows.<ref name="Legacy">''[[Star Wars: The Legacy Collection]]''</ref> Qiraash facial features otherwise resembled those of Humans<ref name="CCG" /> with high [[Bone/Legends|cheekbones]].<ref name="Duel">''[[The Clone Wars: Secret Missions 3: Duel at Shattered Rock]]''</ref>

The Qiraash were unable naturally to [[Hybrid/Legends|interbreed]] with members of the Human species; however, with a certain amount of genetic manipulation, such couplings could produce viable offspring.<ref name="Night">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref> One Qiraash, Leesub Sirln, had limited [[Precognition/Legends|precognition]] powers; these were interpreted by [[High Inquisitor]] [[Antinnis Tremayne]] as [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]].<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|leesubsirln|Sirln, Leesub}}</ref>

==History==
The Qiraash were known in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] from at least [[84 BBY/Legends|84 BBY]], when Qiraash [[Doffen Gaitag]] oversaw construction of the [[Space station/Legends|space station]] known as [[The Wheel/Legends|the Wheel]], which quickly became one of the most popular [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] dens in the galaxy. Gaitag eventually sold the Wheel to the [[J'feh/Legends|J'feh]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Skijid Vrescot]], and his granddaughter, [[Qimberly Gaitag-Delio]], went on to become a celebrity [[Lawyer/Legends|attorney]] nicknamed "the Devourer".<ref name="VSV">{{SW|url=news/viva-space-vegas-the-history-of-the-marvelous-wheel-part-1|series=Viva Space Vegas! The History of the Marvelous Wheel|text=Part 1|nolive=1}}</ref> At one time, the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Wallanooga]]<ref name="Night" />&mdash;a [[Slavery/Legends|slaver]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]<ref name="Hutt! Hutt! Hutt!">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031120hutt|text=Hutt! Hutt! Hutt! #6}}</ref>&mdash;speculated that his slave [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]] might have been a Qiraash/Human hybrid, despite the inability of the Qiraash genome to account for her longevity.<ref name="Night" /> Also during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a [[Unidentified Qiraash bartender|Qiraash]] served as a [[Bartender/Legends|bartender]] at a [[Unidentified Vaced tavern|tavern]] on the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] planet [[Vaced/Legends|Vaced]].<ref name="Duel" />

A full-blooded Qiraash was the female Leesub Sirln, who was enslaved while only a [[Youngling/Legends|youngling]]. During the administration of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Sirln encountered High Inquisitor Tremayne, who,<ref name="DB" /> suspecting the woman had precognition powers, declared her a [[Force Adept]].<ref name="Legacy" /> The [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]] was charged with hunting down [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and other Force-sensitives and either turning them to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] or eliminating them.<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force real-life book">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> Consequently, to avoid [[Prison/Legends|imprisonment]] or [[Death/Legends|death]], Sirln fled to the remote [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where she hid for many years in the town of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]].<ref name="DB" /> She was present in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] when [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] chartered the services of [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] for transit to [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Qiraash_sketch.jpg|thumb|right|upright|An early production sketch of Leesub Sirln]]
Only one Qiraash has appeared in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]]: Leesub Sirln. Originally identified only as "Weird Girl" in the production notes for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], she was filmed in London as an extra for the cantina scene. She can be glimpsed briefly in the film just behind Kenobi and Skywalker in Chalmun's Cantina.<ref name="SW.com">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> An early cut of the cantina sequence shows her more prominently, talking to [[Hrchek Kal Fas/Legends|Hrchek Kal Fas]] at the bar,<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> and a production photo shows her standing in front of the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], but these images were never part of the film.<ref name="SW.com" />

Sirln's name and identification as a Qiraash did not occur until [[1995]] with the release of the of the [[Premiere Limited|first set]] of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]],<ref name="SW.com" /> in which she appears as a Light Side card.<ref name="CCG" /> In addition to mentions in reference sources such as the ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', as well as some [[StarWars.com]] features, the Qiraash are also mentioned in [[Michael Reaves]]' ''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]'', published in [[2008]]. In [[2009]], Sirln received an action figure as part of ''[[Star Wars: The Legacy Collection]]'', and in [[2011]], a second Qiraash character was created by [[Ryder Windham]] for his young reader book ''[[The Clone Wars: Secret Missions 3: Duel at Shattered Rock]]''.

"[[Dining at Dex's]]," a [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]]-exclusive article released in 2009 mentioned [[Qiraadish]]es. The article's author, [[Gregory Walker]], confirmed this was a play on the word "Qiraash".<ref name="JCF">{{JCFCite|url=posts/30604186|board=Literature|thread=Hyperspace New Short Fiction: "The Forgotten War" & "Dining at Dex's" now online!|user=[[Gregory Walker|NarbFlick]]|date=2009-12-06|time=10:29 AM|archiveurl=https://boards.theforce.net/threads/hyperspace-new-short-fiction-jjms-the-secret-journal-of-doctor-demagol-now-online.28297369/page-13#post-30604186}}</ref> The [[in-universe]] connection between the vegetable and the species is not clear.
